edge_explainer: FRAME TEST FIRST, and it inverts: copper is at a 52-week high (+50.8% y/y, COPX +101.8%) while CAML is -1.5% y/y and -33.6% over six months, and CAML's own realised copper price rose 39% in H1-2026. The drawdown is 100% idiosyncratic, so the AEM commodity frame-reject does NOT apply - but that is worse for the bull, not better: the market singled CAML out while re-rating every peer, and it was right to. Cause is fully read: -13.4% on 10-Sep-2025 (interim dividend cut 9p->4.5p), -23.8% on 03-Mar-2026 (Sasa Ore Reserve statement cutting mine life five years to 2034 and the reserve 25% to 6.9Mt), -6.4%/-2.6% on 19/20-Mar-2026 (FY25 results, $117.8M Sasa impairment), and -12% over 02-08 Jun-2026 (the all-scrip Cygnus acquisition, ~79M new shares, ~30% dilution). THE CENTRAL FINDING: both producing assets terminate in the SAME year, 2034 - Kounrad is 'licensed to 2034' with cash flows 'projected until 2034, the remaining life of operation' (AR2025 goodwill note), Sasa's LOM is 'estimated to 2034', and the accounts state neither extends beyond 2040. EV/EBIT is a perpetuity statistic; at an 8.5-year life and 12% discount the annuity factor is 5.15 vs a perpetuity 8.33, so the shelf's headline 4.3x EV/EBIT is economically ~7.0x for a going concern - still cheap, not top-decile, and mis-ranked against non-extractive names. That is a shelf-wide lesson: the deep-value composite mechanically over-ranks finite-life miners (applies to THX #1 and SRB #3 too). Two SCREEN REFUTATIONS: (a) the share count is 177,710,956 (Total Voting Rights RNS 31-Mar-2026), 3-4% above the shelf's 172.09M and yfinance's 170.4M, raising market cap to $353.6M; (b) the '4.3x EBIT' uses a VENDOR-adjusted EBIT of $63.5M against a reported operating LOSS of $49.6M. HONESTY GRADE CLEAN: CAML pre-announced the reserve cut in a standalone RNS sixteen days ahead of results, took the impairment immediately and in full, cut the dividend TO its stated 30-50%-of-FCF policy rather than borrowing to hold it, and disclosed that its own Kounrad dump estimates had been too conservative. A genuinely impaired-life business that discloses its impairment promptly is CLEAN; the only takeaway-vs-data divergence in this file is in the screen, not the company. WHAT YOU ARE PAID FOR: an 8.19% trailing yield (IBKR field; 12p/148p) with 0% UK withholding, policy-bound at 30-50% of FCF, on a balance sheet with net cash that GREW $78.7M -> $96.7M in H1-2026 after a completed $10M buyback, plus a confirmed structural tailwind the trailing screen cannot contain: Kazakhstan cut the Mineral Extraction Tax on man-made formations including Kounrad from 8.55% to 0.855% effective 1-Jan-2026, worth ~$13M/yr pre-tax (~13% of FY25 group EBITDA), only partly offset by dividend WHT rising 10%->15%. Capital commitments are only $6.6M (the THX pre-committed-FCF test passes clean) and there is no UK DB scheme or equity-inflating surplus (the addendum's pension-by-hand test passes clean). WHAT YOU ARE NOT PAID FOR: earnings at a 52-week-high copper price when management's OWN impairment model uses a long-term deck of $10,767/t, 27% below spot; a Sasa orebody the company describes as 'narrower... more variable in both geometry and grade' at depth with head grades down 9-10% y/y; and a 30% all-scrip dilution at 156p to buy a pre-production, zero-revenue Quebec project with NO published economic study - which transfers roughly 10-15p per share and inverts the usual arb sign, making deal FAILURE the bull case (pre-deal intrinsic ~187p vs post-deal ~172p). RULING: neither a clean de-rate nor a derailment but a MANDATE CHANGE on a wasting asset - the 2026 earnings trajectory is rising hard (de-rate signature) while the reserve trajectory is falling (derailment signature), and the security has converted from a high-payout runoff yield vehicle into a Quebec copper developer, so the holders who owned the old mandate are the sellers and the holders who want the new one have not arrived. At E[FV] 167p vs 148p the price edge is only ~12.5%, which with a ~6.2% net-of-tax yield gives ~18%/yr in the base case against a -20% bear - fairly-paid risk with a thin edge overlay from the MET cut and the annuity-vs-perpetuity framing gap, not a mispricing. Sized at the UK 0.75% cap the position is a token; its real value is that a ~30bp round trip on a 14bp touch and $1.5M of median daily turnover makes CAML the one name on this shelf cheap enough to prove the venue with.
